```python
from apache_beam.options.pipeline_options import PipelineOptions
with beam.Pipeline(options=PipelineOptions()) as p:
  (p
   | 'Read' >> beam.io.ReadFromPubSub(topic=topic)
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical, beginner-friendly use of Google-native services to automate a nightly job and monitor it end-to-end.

- Cloud Run Jobs for batch tasks
- Artifact Registry as image store
- Cloud Scheduler for time-based triggers

## Code Example

```javascript
# Build and push image
gcloud auth configure-docker us-central1-docker.pkg.dev
docker build -t daily-processor:latest .
docker tag daily-processor:latest us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT/REPO/daily-processor:latest
docker push us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT/REPO/daily-processor:latest

# Deploy Cloud Run Job
gcloud run jobs create daily-processor --image us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT/REPO/daily-processor:latest --region us-central1

  --schedule "0 2 * * *" \
  --time-zone "UTC" \
  --http-method POST \
  --uri "https://run.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT/locations/us-central1/jobs/daily-processor:run" \
  --oauth-service-account-email service-account@PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com

# Manual test

```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design advanced traffic routing using header-based rules and serverless NEGs, enabling cohort-driven canaries without modifying application code paths. Emphasizes per-cohort monitoring, safe rollback procedures, and Google-native tooling integration.

## Key Concepts
- Header-based routing with URL maps and traffic weights
- Serverless NEGs and Cloud Run service management
- Per-cohort traffic distribution and rollback strategies
- Cloud Monitoring metrics and SLO evaluation
- IAM role management and Secret Manager integration

## Code Example
```yaml
# Example URL map configuration for header-based routing
name: cohort-based-url-map
defaultService: https://www.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/project-id/global/backendServices/v2-backend

hostRules:
- hosts: ['*']
  pathMatcher: cohort-matcher

pathMatchers:
- name: cohort-matcher
  defaultService: https://www.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/project-id/global/backendServices/v2-backend
  routeRules:
  - matchRules:
    - headers:
        X-User-Cohort: A
    priority: 1
    routeAction:
      weightedBackendServices:
      - backendService: https://www.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/project-id/global/backendServices/v3-backend
        weight: 20
      - backendService: https://www.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/project-id/global/backendServices/v2-backend
        weight: 80
  - matchRules:
    - headers:
        X-User-Cohort: B
    priority: 2
    routeAction:
      weightedBackendServices:
      - backendService: https://www.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/project-id/global/backendServices/v2-backend
        weight: 100
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical CI/CD skills for Cloud Run using Google-native tools. It evaluates understanding of the complete deployment pipeline, including build, test, deploy, manual promotion gates, and IAM least-privilege configurations.

## Key Concepts
- Cloud Build triggers configured on Git push events
- Artifact Registry for Docker image storage and versioning
- Cloud Run deployment with environment promotion (dev → staging → prod)
- IAM role bindings following least-privilege principles
- Manual approval gates for production deployments

## Solution Overview

**1. Create Artifact Registry repository:**
```bash
gcloud artifacts repositories create inventory-sync \
  --repository-format=docker \
  --location=us-central1
```

**2. Create Cloud Build trigger for dev:**
```bash
gcloud builds triggers create github \
  --name=inventory-sync-dev \
  --repo=inventory-sync \
  --branch-pattern=^main$ \
  --build-config=cloudbuild.yaml
```

**3. cloudbuild.yaml:**
```yaml
steps:
  - name: 'gcr.io/cloud-builders/docker'
    args: ['build', '-t', 'us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/$PROJECT_ID/inventory-sync/inventory-sync:$COMMIT_SHA', '.']

  - name: 'gcr.io/cloud-builders/docker'
    args: ['push', 'us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/$PROJECT_ID/inventory-sync/inventory-sync:$COMMIT_SHA']

  - name: 'gcr.io/google.com/cloudsdktool/cloud-sdk'
    entrypoint: gcloud
    args: ['run', 'deploy', 'inventory-sync-dev', '--image', 'us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/$PROJECT_ID/inventory-sync/inventory-sync:$COMMIT_SHA', '--region', 'us-central1', '--platform', 'managed']

  - name: 'gcr.io/cloud-builders/npm'
    args: ['test']

images:
  - 'us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/$PROJECT_ID/inventory-sync/inventory-sync:$COMMIT_SHA'
```

**4. Create production trigger with manual approval:**
```bash
gcloud builds triggers create github \
  --name=inventory-sync-prod \
  --repo=inventory-sync \
  --tag-pattern=^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+$ \
  --build-config=cloudbuild-prod.yaml
```

**5. Minimal IAM roles for Cloud Build SA:**
```bash
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding $PROJECT_ID \
  --member=serviceAccount:$PROJECT_NUMBER@cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role='roles/run.developer'

gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding $PROJECT_ID \
  --member=serviceAccount:$PROJECT_NUMBER@cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role='roles/artifactregistry.writer'

gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding $PROJECT_ID \
  --member=serviceAccount:$PROJECT_NUMBER@cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role='roles/logging.logWriter'
```

## Key Takeaways
This pipeline demonstrates a production-ready GitOps workflow with proper separation between dev and production environments. The manual approval stage (via tag-based triggers in Cloud Build) ensures that production deployments are intentional and reviewed. The IAM configuration follows the principle of least privilege by granting only the permissions required for each task.
